Class

Algebra 1

Explore Algebra 1 through the world of mountain biking. Learn how equations, graphs, and mathematical relationships help explain speed, elevation, jumps, and trail design.

9 units · 42 topics · 1 learning activity

Units

  1. Unit 1 Foundations of Algebra 4 topics

    1. Variables and Expressions

      Use letters to stand for quantities that change, and write expressions that describe a situation.

      • Write an expression from a description in words
      • Identify variables, coefficients, constants and terms
      • Explain what an expression means in context
      Activities in development

    2. Evaluating Expressions

      Substitute values for variables and work out the result.

      • Substitute values into an expression
      • Evaluate expressions with negatives, fractions and decimals
      • Evaluate real-world formulas
      Activities in development

    3. Order of Operations

      Apply the agreed order (grouping, exponents, multiplication and division, addition and subtraction) so every expression has one value.

      • Simplify numerical expressions using the order of operations
      • Work with parentheses, brackets and fraction bars
      • Find and fix order-of-operations mistakes
      Activities in development

    4. Properties of Real Numbers

      Use the commutative, associative, distributive, identity and inverse properties to rewrite and simplify expressions.

      • Classify numbers as natural, whole, integer, rational or irrational
      • Identify and use the commutative, associative and identity properties
      • Use the distributive property to expand and combine like terms
      Activities in development
  2. Unit 2 Solving Equations and Inequalities 5 topics

    1. One-Step Equations

      Undo a single operation to find the value of a variable.

      • Solve equations using inverse operations
      • Check a solution by substitution
      • Write and solve a one-step equation from a situation
      Activities in development

    2. Multi-Step Equations

      Combine like terms, distribute and undo operations in order to solve equations with several steps.

      • Solve equations that need two or more steps
      • Distribute and combine like terms before solving
      • Write and solve multi-step equations from situations
      Activities in development

    3. Variables on Both Sides

      Collect variable terms on one side to solve equations where the variable appears twice, including ones with no solution or infinitely many.

      • Solve equations with variables on both sides
      • Recognize equations with no solution or infinitely many solutions
      • Solve “when are they equal” problems
      Activities in development

    4. Literal Equations

      Rearrange a formula to solve for a different variable.

      • Solve a formula for a given variable
      • Rearrange real-world formulas (d = rt, grade = rise / run)
      • Use a rearranged formula to answer a question
      Activities in development

    5. Inequalities

      Solve and graph inequalities, remembering to flip the sign when multiplying or dividing by a negative.

      • Solve one- and multi-step inequalities
      • Graph solutions on a number line
      • Solve and interpret compound inequalities
      • Write inequalities for real-world limits
      Activities in development
  3. Unit 3 Linear Relationships 6 topics · 3 with activities

    1. Coordinate Plane

      Locate points using an x- and y-axis, and describe the four quadrants.

      • Identify the axes, origin and quadrants
      • Read the coordinates of a point
      • Read graphs whose axes use different scales
      Activities in development

    2. Graphing Ordered Pairs

      Plot points from ordered pairs and tables, and read patterns in them.

      • Plot ordered pairs on a coordinate plane
      • Graph a table of values
      • Describe a pattern in plotted points
      Activities in development

    3. Slope and Rate of Change

      Slope measures how much one quantity changes for each unit of change in another: rise over run.

      • Understand slope as a rate of change
      • Calculate slope using two points
      • Interpret positive and negative slope
      • Understand slope in real-world scenarios, including percentage grade
      1 activity

    4. Positive and Negative Slope

      Classify slopes as positive, negative, zero or undefined, and connect each to the direction of a line.

      • Classify a slope as positive, negative, zero or undefined
      • Connect the sign of slope to the direction of a line
      • Explain why a vertical line has undefined slope
      1 activity

    5. Linear Relationships

      Recognize a constant rate of change in tables, graphs, equations and situations.

      • Recognize a constant rate of change
      • Decide whether a table is linear
      • Connect tables, graphs, equations and words
      1 activity

    6. Proportional Relationships

      Relationships of the form y = kx: a constant ratio, and a line through the origin.

      • Find the constant of proportionality
      • Decide whether a relationship is proportional
      • Write and use y = kx
      Activities in development
  4. Unit 4 Linear Equations and Functions 6 topics · 3 with activities

    1. Writing Linear Equations

      Write the equation of a line from a slope and a point, two points, a table, a graph or a description.

      • Write an equation from a slope and a point
      • Write an equation from two points
      • Write an equation from a real-world description
      1 activity

    2. Slope-Intercept Form

      y = mx + b: read the slope m and y-intercept b, and use them to graph.

      • Identify slope and y-intercept from y = mx + b
      • Explain what m and b mean in context
      • Rewrite an equation in slope-intercept form
      1 activity

    3. Point-Slope Form

      y − y₁ = m(x − x₁): write a line from any point on it and its slope.

      • Write an equation in point-slope form
      • Convert between point-slope and slope-intercept form
      • Choose a useful form for a problem
      Activities in development

    4. Graphing Linear Equations

      Graph lines from slope and intercept, from intercepts, or from a table.

      • Graph a line from its slope and y-intercept
      • Graph using x- and y-intercepts
      • Graph horizontal and vertical lines
      1 activity

    5. Domain and Range

      Describe the inputs and outputs that make sense for a function.

      • Find domain and range from a graph, table or set of pairs
      • Choose a reasonable domain for a real-world model
      • Write domain and range with inequalities or interval notation
      Activities in development

    6. Function Notation

      Use f(x) to name functions, evaluate them, and interpret statements like f(3) = 12.

      • Decide whether a relation is a function
      • Evaluate functions written in f(x) notation
      • Interpret function notation in context
      Activities in development
  5. Unit 5 Systems of Equations 4 topics

    1. Graphing Systems

      Solve two linear equations at once by finding where their graphs meet.

      • Solve a system by graphing
      • Recognize systems with one, none or infinitely many solutions
      • Interpret the intersection point in context
      Activities in development

    2. Substitution

      Solve a system by replacing one variable with an expression from the other equation.

      • Solve a system by substitution
      • Choose which variable to substitute
      • Check a solution in both equations
      Activities in development

    3. Elimination

      Add or subtract equations (after scaling if needed) to eliminate a variable.

      • Solve a system by elimination
      • Multiply equations to line up coefficients
      • Choose between graphing, substitution and elimination
      Activities in development

    4. Applications of Systems

      Model situations with two unknowns and solve them.

      • Write a system from a situation
      • Solve break-even and comparison problems
      • Solve mixture and rate problems
      Activities in development
  6. Unit 6 Exponents and Exponential Relationships 4 topics

    1. Exponent Rules

      Multiply, divide and raise powers; work with zero and negative exponents.

      • Use the product and quotient rules
      • Use power of a power and power of a product
      • Simplify zero and negative exponents
      Activities in development

    2. Scientific Notation

      Write very large and very small numbers as a × 10ⁿ, and compute with them.

      • Convert between standard and scientific notation
      • Multiply and divide in scientific notation
      • Compare quantities in scientific notation
      Activities in development

    3. Exponential Growth

      Model quantities that grow by the same percent each period: y = a(1 + r)ˣ.

      • Identify exponential growth from tables, graphs and equations
      • Write a growth model from a starting value and rate
      • Tell linear growth from exponential growth
      Activities in development

    4. Exponential Decay

      Model quantities that shrink by the same percent each period: y = a(1 − r)ˣ.

      • Identify exponential decay
      • Write a decay model
      • Estimate when a decaying quantity reaches a target
      Activities in development
  7. Unit 7 Polynomials and Factoring 4 topics

    1. Adding and Subtracting Polynomials

      Name polynomials by degree and number of terms, and add or subtract them.

      • Classify polynomials by degree and number of terms
      • Add polynomials
      • Subtract polynomials, distributing the negative
      Activities in development

    2. Multiplying Polynomials

      Multiply monomials, binomials and polynomials, including special products.

      • Multiply binomials
      • Use square-of-a-sum and difference-of-squares patterns
      • Multiply polynomials with more terms
      Activities in development

    3. Factoring Expressions

      Factor out the greatest common factor and factor by grouping.

      • Factor out the greatest common factor
      • Factor by grouping
      • Check factoring by multiplying back
      Activities in development

    4. Factoring Quadratics

      Factor trinomials like x² + bx + c and ax² + bx + c, and special patterns.

      • Factor x² + bx + c
      • Factor ax² + bx + c
      • Factor perfect squares and differences of squares
      Activities in development
  8. Unit 8 Quadratic Equations and Functions 5 topics

    1. Graphing Quadratics

      Graph y = ax² + bx + c and describe its parabola: opening direction, width, intercepts.

      • Graph a quadratic function
      • Describe how a changes the parabola
      • Read intercepts and the maximum or minimum from a graph
      Activities in development

    2. Vertex and Axis of Symmetry

      Find the vertex and axis of symmetry of a parabola, and interpret the vertex as a maximum or minimum.

      • Find the vertex using x = −b / 2a
      • Find and use the axis of symmetry
      • Interpret the vertex in context
      Activities in development

    3. Factoring Quadratics

      Solve quadratic equations by factoring and the zero-product property.

      • Solve quadratics using the zero-product property
      • Rewrite in standard form before factoring
      • Interpret the solutions in context
      Activities in development

    4. Quadratic Formula

      Solve any quadratic with x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) / 2a, and use the discriminant.

      • Solve quadratics with the quadratic formula
      • Use the discriminant to count real solutions
      • Choose a solving method
      Activities in development

    5. Applications of Quadratic Functions

      Use quadratic models for projectile motion, area and optimization.

      • Solve projectile-motion problems
      • Find maximum and minimum values in context
      • Decide which solutions make sense
      Activities in development
  9. Unit 9 Data and Statistics 4 topics

    1. Data Representation

      Display and summarize data with dot plots, histograms and box plots, using center and spread.

      • Choose and make an appropriate data display
      • Find mean, median, range and interquartile range
      • Compare two data sets
      Activities in development

    2. Scatter Plots

      Plot paired data to look for relationships between two variables.

      • Make a scatter plot from paired data
      • Describe the direction and form of an association
      • Spot outliers and clusters
      Activities in development

    3. Correlation

      Describe how strongly two variables move together, and why correlation is not causation.

      • Describe correlation as positive, negative or none, strong or weak
      • Interpret a correlation coefficient
      • Explain why correlation doesn’t prove causation
      Activities in development

    4. Lines of Best Fit

      Fit a line to data, interpret its slope and intercept, and use it to predict.

      • Draw or calculate a line of best fit
      • Interpret its slope and intercept in context
      • Make predictions and judge them with residuals
      Activities in development
